rows.why: S1 depends on what the default share is when none is configured. Item 7 asks this and picks a default of 7500 bps, which gives a 7500 release from a 10000 bounty.
Item 2 asks how an uneven split is rounded. It picks BigInt integer division rounded down, with UAT taking the remainder. That gives 749 and 250, and stays exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.
Item 12 asks what the UAT release amount is. It picks the bounty minus the hidden-test amount, which is the remaining balance S3 expects.
Item 8 asks what a failed hidden-test run does. It picks returning the current state without writing, so nothing is recorded and the task stays locked.

Item 1 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. It picks throwing an Error and recording nothing, which matches. The pick doesn't give the error message, but the refusal itself matches.
Item 4 asks about the status and releases for a zero bounty. It uses "pro bono" but still records a release of 0 on hidden-test pass. S6 says no release is ever recorded.
Item 3 asks about repeat deliveries, including the same kind with a new event id. It treats any later event of an already-released kind as a no-op, whatever the id, which covers both parts of S7.
Item 10 asks how concurrent duplicate events are handled. It picks a per-handler promise queue, so simultaneous events run one after another and only one release is recorded.
Item 10 also asks how store failures are handled. It lets store errors reject without recording anything and keeps the queue usable, so a retry succeeds.
